ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development

BENBUSI112.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance

BENBUSI211.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
BENBUSI211.contribution: analyses the effect of AI on competitiveness, innovation, labour markets and society and examines AI governance and ethics across marketing, human resources and finance; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the management of business information and responsible management in the target, without teaching information-systems management itself
BENBUSI211.topics: AI capabilities and limitations; AI in business functions and industries; Agentic AI; Market structure and business models; Automation and augmentation; Labour markets and productivity; Innovation and economic growth; Inequality; Techno-economic paradigms and economic narratives; AI ethics and societal impacts; Corporate governance and AI regulation; National AI readiness and industrial policy; Future AI scenarios

BENBUSI311.name: Transnational Business Law
BENBUSI311.contribution: introduces the legal frameworks of cross-border trade, contracts, sales of goods and services, intellectual property, foreign investment and dispute resolution; it directly implements the business-law element that the programme names alongside taxation and ethics, without teaching tax law
BENBUSI311.topics: International trade regulation; Comparative and international contract law; International sales; Transport of goods and Incoterms; Documentary transactions; International trade finance; Employment and sale of services; Intellectual-property protection; International commercial dispute resolution; Foreign direct investment; E-commerce and digital economy regulation
BENBUSI311.methods: Comparative legal analysis; Application of legal rules to commercial scenarios; Transport-risk allocation analysis; Intellectual-property strategy assessment; E-commerce legal-compliance analysis; Arbitration memorandum drafting and simulated advocacy

BENBUSI312.name: Money, Banking & Finance
BENBUSI312.contribution: develops financial decision-making through case studies in which students analyse financial data, assess risk and take investment, budgeting and business decisions; it directly addresses the financial decision-making of the target's Finance and Managerial Finance and Accounting, without a full corporate-finance theory sequence

BENBUSI312.methods: Algebraic and graphical financial analysis; Balance-sheet analysis; Duration gap analysis; Bank-management simulation (Stanford Banking Game); Excel-based financial dashboard construction and performance analysis; Financial-statement forecasting; Research-article extension using literature comparison, case study or updated data

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics

BENECON211.name: International Macroeconomics
BENECON211.contribution: studies national income, growth, inflation, unemployment, fiscal and monetary policy, business cycles, crises and international trade; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the international economic environment that the target addresses in Economics and Business and Global Business, at the level of national economies rather than firms
BENECON211.topics: Goods and financial markets; Labour markets; Phillips curve; IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models; Economic growth; Saving and capital accumulation; Technological progress; Expectations; Open-economy macroeconomics; Fiscal and monetary policy; Business cycles and economic crises

BENECON311.name: Public Economics

BENECON311.topics: Role and size of government; Market efficiency and failure; Public goods; Externalities; Efficiency and equity; Public production; Public choice; Public expenditure; Health and education policy; Welfare programs; Social insurance; Taxation and redistribution

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.contribution: teaches ordinary and generalised least squares and instrumental variables estimators, t, F and LM tests, Monte Carlo simulation in Stata and an empirical paper; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's quantitative-methods line and to its thesis preparation at greater econometric depth
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design

BENENTR211.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement

BENENTR211.topics: Strategic marketing planning; Marketing mix; Customer centricity and experience; Consumer journeys; Market research and augmented insights; Brand identity and image; Brand partnerships; Digital and social marketing; Responsible marketing; Consumer psychology; Nudging and framing; Emerging technologies and marketing agility

BENENTR212.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation

BENENTR212.topics: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society. Organisation, leadership and cross-cultural communication (Organisation major)
Supply chain management and operations (Supply Chain Management major)

analysis: The closest plan offers direct international trade, institutions and cross-border governance, accounting, asset markets, strategy, marketing, market research and entrepreneurship. Design adds user needs, prototypes and production scaling, while life-cycle analysis adds resource and supply implications. Database management offers concrete data design and SQL rather than a management-information-systems sequence. Research Methods & Statistics offers inference and regression and overlaps the applied statistics course. The emerging economies option retains economics, econometrics, entrepreneurship, governance and business law and adds concrete tools for comparative institutions, colonial and economic legacies, conflict risk, redistribution, development and sustainability. Agricultural systems supply a sector application. Psychology of Leading Under Pressure contributes culturally informed emotion regulation and psychological safety. The thirteen-course separation each way changes the programme from firm functions to how institutions and development condition international business. Organisation coverage already includes applied negotiation and organisational psychology. Specialist supply networks and operations are insufficient for a further coherent option. Preserved the two valid concepts after retiming Business & Economy in the Age of AI and Consumer Product Design and their necessary counterpart.

alignment.rationale: Both address how organisations function and are managed; Psychology of Organizations & Leadership approaches this through organisational behaviour, motivation, group dynamics, culture and leadership, rather than through management theory or organisational design.

Both address marketing management; Marketing & Consumer Engagement covers consumer behaviour, marketing strategy, digital marketing and brand strategy with marketing plans, without a cross-country focus.
Both address business strategy; Strategy & Digital Transformation has students develop a strategic plan from vision to execution, with a digital-technology emphasis.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Management of Organisations and Marketing introduces organisations and marketing together; the UCR courses on each half are aligned with the larger Management of Organisations and Marketing Management components, and no further UCR course is a sufficiently direct counterpart.

Both develop leadership skills; Personal Leadership introduces transformational and authentic leadership with self-awareness and practical skills, which is the specific function of the Professional Development: Leadership Skills training, although it is a full course rather than a short training.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Management Game is a team-based management simulation skills training, and no scheduled UCR course is a sufficiently direct counterpart; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations is a venture-creation course aligned with Entrepreneurship and Small Business Management.
Both teach financial reporting; Accounting & Corporate Finance covers accounting theory and practice with emphasis on using and analysing financial statements and annual reports.
Both study financial markets, asset pricing, and risk and return. Maastricht also develops the corporate investment perspective.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Managerial Finance and Accounting is a second-year course on management accounting and corporate finance; UCR's accounting and finance courses are already aligned with Accounting and Financial Reporting and Finance, and no other UCR course addresses managerial accounting.

Both give the economic foundations for business; Introduction to Economics covers micro- and macroeconomics, which is the economics part of Economics and Business, without the business-context applications.

Both address international business; International Business & Governance examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses, global trade and cross-border governance, which is the central subject of Global Business.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Corporate Governance is a dedicated second-year course on the governance of firms; International Business & Governance covers cross-border governance but is already aligned with Global Business, and no other scheduled UCR course addresses corporate governance.
UCR takes a consumer product from needs to prototype and considers production scaling. Maastricht also develops quantitative methods for operations and supply decisions.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Fundamentals of Supply Chain Management has no UCR counterpart; Life Cycle Analysis & Circular Economy addresses the life cycle of products from raw materials to reuse but not logistics, sourcing or supply-chain management.
UCR develops database design, SQL and data management skills. Maastricht studies how organisations use information systems for business processes and strategy.

Both address starting and running a small venture; Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations has teams develop a venture from idea to final pitch with market validation and business planning, without the small-business management content of the component.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Quantitative Methods I (EBC1005).
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Quantitative Methods II (EBC1033).
Both use statistical inference and regression to analyse data. Maastricht’s skills course applies these methods to business case studies.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Philosophy of Science (EBS1001, skills training).
